subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & recent regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really enjoyed learning more about your search/QA flows and the fine-grained phrasing issues you've been seeing on product descriptions. Below is a short recap and recommended next steps so we can validate fit quickly.

Recap
- Goal: Improve relevance + factuality for product description Q&A and inline search suggestions.
- Current pain: high false positives on short queries, occasional hallucinations on SKU attributes.

Redwood recommendations (first-pass) - Model: redwood-instruct-1.3-std (balanced latency/cost for retrieval-augmented prompts)
- For high-precision SKU attribute extraction tests: redwood-instruct-1.3-large (higher compute, better context)
- Prompt set: see attached "acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx" (includes 120 seed prompts across categories: short-query, multi-turn clarification, SKU extraction)
- Benchmarks: full benchmark and QA evals uploaded here: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-retail-2026-07

Quality/regression note (preventative)
- We saw regressions in other retail customers when models moved from v1.2 -> v1.3 with a different decoding config. We recommend pinning model versions for the initial eval and agreeing on roll-forward criteria (quality thresholds on your seed prompt set).

Attachments
- acme_benchmark_report_2026-07.pdf (summary metrics and error examples)
- acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx (seed prompts + expected outputs)

Next steps
1) Marcus + Ethan to run a quick eval on 50 priority prompts from the attached set and share diff vs your baseline by EOD Fri (we can run in our sandbox).
2) Alice/Tom to confirm which routes you want included (Search autocomplete + Product Q&A) and whether you want strict precision or recall prioritization.
3) If we observe regressions tied to a model variant, we will propose either pinning to v1.2 for production traffic or a targeted rollback while we investigate.

If this looks good I'll schedule Marcus/Ethan for the sandbox run and share a short plan for canary rollout options.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Thanks Marissa — I'll take point on the sandbox eval. Quick notes from SRE/SE perspective after glancing at the prompt set:
- We'll run the 50-priority prompt batch under two model configs: redwood-instruct-1.3-std (default) and redwood-instruct-1.2-std (pinned baseline) so we can diff results and surface regressions.
- If we see a measurable drop (>8% accuracy on SKU extraction or >12% decrease in precision on short queries), recommend holding v1.3 for production and keeping v1.2 pinned until root cause is identified.
- I'll attach a small script and a set of diff metrics (precision, recall, F1, hallucination rate) in the sandbox run results.

Marcus
Marcus Lin | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeretail.com>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Confirming: include both Search autocomplete and Product Q&A routes and prioritize precision for SKU attributes (precision > 90% is our main requirement).

A couple quick asks:
- Can you share the diff report format ahead of the run so our engineers can align on success criteria?
- If you recommend pinning, how fast can that be applied to our Dedicated environment? We need minimal user-facing impact during the holiday flash-sale next month.

Thanks — we'll review the attached prompt set today and circle back if we have any edits.

Best,
Alice
Product Ops | Acme Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (model recommendations & prompt sets)

Thanks Alice — noted on precision > 90% and routes. Marcus/Ethan: please share the diff-report template and sandbox run schedule by noon PT so Acme can review.

Quick answers to the environment question:
- Pinning: we can pin traffic to an older model version at the routing layer immediately for Dedicated customers (config change, no deploy) — typical lead time: 15-60 minutes to apply and validate.
- Rollback: if the regression is caused by a model variant we pushed, we can rollback to the pinned model and open an engineering investigation; rollback timeline depends on the root cause but the traffic switch is similarly fast.

Action items
- Marcus/Ethan: run the 50-priority prompt eval and upload the diff report to the drive link.
- Marissa: I'll coordinate a short call next week with your engineering leads if the diff shows >8% regression on SKU extraction.

I'll also open an internal ticket with our incident team to flag this as a regression-risk eval for Acme (will include the benchmark PDF and prompt set).

Cheers,
Marissa
